description: Live playback on the running engine: notes, modes, the keyboard sweep, MIDI files, reset.

commands.name: play.note
commands.title: Play a note
commands.description: Note-on / note-off / sustain event on the live engine. pitch = MIDI note number = preset pitch id (keys 21-108; output pitches >= 128 never sound). velocity 0-127 MIDI; command 144 = NOTE_ON (velocity 0 = NOTE_OFF), 128 = NOTE_OFF, 176-178 with pitch 64 = sustain pedal.

source.description: 'midi' = hardware MIDI input: the Fix-MIDI velocity clamp applies

commands.name: play.mode
commands.title: Play a resonance mode
commands.description: Immediate playback of one resonance mode (debug builds return the mode-state record).

commands.name: play.keyboard
commands.title: Play the keyboard sweep (live)
commands.description: Schedules a NOTE_ON/NOTE_OFF sweep over the keyboard on the live driver and returns immediately. With capture_mic the call blocks until the microphone capture ends.

speed_ms_per_note.description: NOTE_ON to NOTE_OFF duration per key, ms

pitches.description: Explicit pitch list; omit for all pitches

tail_ms.description: Extra capture after the last NOTE_OFF, ms

commands.name: play.midi_file
commands.title: Play a MIDI file
commands.description: Starts online playback of a bundled MIDI file. Long-running: returns a jobId; the job finishes when playback completes or is stopped (job.cancel or play.midi_file_stop).

start_delay_ms.description: Delay before the first event, ms

commands.name: play.reset
commands.title: Reset the engine state
commands.description: Re-initialises the simulation state (silences ringing notes) without reloading the preset.

commands.name: midi.ports
commands.title: Read the MIDI input ports
commands.description: The rtmidi input ports (array index = port id), the port the unified MIDI listener holds open (active_port, null when not listening or in Listen to All), whether the listener runs (listening; it starts with a load with listen_to_midi 1) and port_state (mode forced / manual / auto / all; ports = the names of every played port: in mode all, every input port merged). Works before a preset is loaded.

commands.name: midi.broadcast_state
commands.title: Read the MIDI broadcast gate
commands.description: Whether incoming MIDI notes are forwarded to the UI as midi_note_event messages ({enabled}). Independent of the listener state (midi.ports). 400 when no preset is loaded.

commands.name: midi.input_settings
commands.title: Read the MIDI pedal settings and live sustain state
commands.description: Which CC is the sustain pedal (sustain_cc, default 64), its polarity ('normal' = value >= 64 is down; 'inverted' = the pedal sends 0 when pressed), show_realtime (clock / active sensing shown in the MIDI monitor), monitor_all_ports (the monitor also shows the input ports the listener does not play from), the sustain state the engine was last sent (sustain_down; sustain_value = last raw value of the sustain CC) and per-type message counts since the backend started. Every incoming message is also pushed to the MIDI monitor as Socket.IO midi_message (raw hex, port, channel). Works before a preset is loaded.

commands.name: midi.set_input_settings
commands.title: Set the MIDI pedal mapping
commands.description: Change any subset of the live MIDI input settings (persisted across backend restarts; applies to the next incoming message). sustain_cc: the CC number the pedal sends (0-127, 64 = standard; read midi.input_settings counts or the MIDI monitor to see what the pedal really sends). sustain_channel: the MIDI channel of the pedal (1-16) or null = any channel; set it when several pedals send the same CC on different channels (e.g. the AMC-10 sends CC 0 from three pedal inputs on channels 1-3; its sustain = CC 0 on channel 2, inverted). polarity: 'inverted' for a pedal that sends 0 when pressed and 127 when released. show_realtime: show MIDI clock / active sensing in the monitor. monitor_all_ports: also monitor the other input ports (applies at the next listener start or port switch). port_sustain: per-port pedal maps {port name: {sustain_cc, sustain_channel, polarity}} (all three per port; replaces the whole map; a port without an entry uses the global sustain_cc / sustain_channel / polarity) - used when several devices are played at once (Listen to All), e.g. the AMC-10: MIDIIN2 (AMC-10) -> sustain_cc 0, sustain_channel 2, polarity inverted. all_exclude: port names Listen to All never opens. The MIDI input PORT (input_port, incl. 'all' = Listen to All) is deliberately not settable here: the user picks it in the MIDI panel (POST /midi/select_port) or auto-detect decides.

sustain_cc.description: CC number of the sustain pedal (64 = standard)

sustain_channel.description: MIDI channel of the sustain pedal (1-16); null = any channel

polarity.description: normal: high value = down; inverted: low value = down (default CC64 pedal: switch at 64; remapped pedal: hysteresis, down at >= 74, up at <= 54 after the polarity)

show_realtime.description: Show clock / active sensing in the MIDI monitor

monitor_all_ports.description: Also monitor the input ports the listener does not play from

port_sustain.description: Per-port pedal maps keyed by port name (rtmidi index suffix optional); replaces the whole map

all_exclude.description: Port names Listen to All never opens

commands.name: controller.status
commands.title: Read the Pianoid controller (pedal inputs, calibration, link speed)
commands.description: Only for the "Pianoid" USB-MIDI controller (FATAR keybed + FPGA + Arduino Micro). present=false when no port named Pianoid is connected. Otherwise: identity (firmware, protocol), the 8 pedal inputs (connector X9-X16, type off / switch / continuous, MIDI message cc / note / channel_pressure / pitch_bend, number, channel 1-16, polarity, calibration curve + min / mid / max raw ADC 0-1023, presence: active = a pedal pulls the input now, seen = it did since the controller booted, idle = only idle-high seen, which is also how an open switch pedal reads), the live raw value, the FPGA -> controller link speed (1x / 4x / 8x; selectable = the bitstream supports switching) and duplicates (inputs that send the same message). Read from the device; nothing is stored in Pianoid. Works before a preset is loaded.

commands.name: controller.set_pedal_message
commands.title: Assign the MIDI message of a Pianoid controller pedal input
commands.description: Set what one pedal input of the Pianoid controller sends (live on the device at once; it survives a power cycle only after controller.save). input: 0-7 (controller.status lists them with their connectors; X12 = input 2 is the sustain pedal by default, X14 = input 0 is CC 67). type: off / switch (0 / 127, or note on / off) / continuous. message: cc (number 0-119; 64 = sustain, 66 = sostenuto, 67 = soft, 11 = expression), note (switch only), channel_pressure, pitch_bend. channel: 1-16. polarity: auto (a switch's level at power-up = released), normal, inverted. The device refuses CC 120-127 (channel-mode messages). Two inputs on the same message are allowed (controller.status reports them as duplicates). Pianoid's sustain pedal is CC 64 on any channel by default (midi.input_settings).

commands.name: controller.set_link_speed
commands.title: Set the Pianoid controller's FPGA link speed
commands.description: The rate of the wire from the controller's FPGA to its USB chip (not the DIN MIDI socket, which is always standard 31250): 1x = 31250, 4x = 125000, 8x = 250000 (default; a chord of 8 notes takes 1 ms on the wire instead of 7.7 ms). Both chips switch together; a switch that does not complete falls back to the previous speed by itself. 409 Unsupported = the FPGA bitstream has no runtime speed switch. Survives a power cycle only after controller.save.

commands.name: controller.save
commands.title: Save the Pianoid controller's configuration
commands.description: Write the controller's current pedal assignments, calibrations and link speed to its EEPROM, so they survive a power cycle (until then a change is live but temporary).
